statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 7 of 100 in the low band, eighteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday is now about thirty-two and a half hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; seventeen of the twenty-four published forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress rises a point to 61 in the elevated band on overnight escalation reports: Iranian state media described two explosions off Qeshm Island inside the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi authorities said a Houthi attack wounded two people and damaged a mosque in Jizan, the Saudi East-West pipeline remains shut with 4 to 5 per cent of global supply off its route, the U.S. average diesel price set a record $6.05 per gallon on Friday and prediction markets price the 16 September FOMC near 79.5 per cent for a 25 basis point increase. Confidence is 87: every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour and the Qeshm reports were confirmed from two independent outlets, while the one missing evidence class remains a live price path that no venue can supply until the scheduled 22:00 UTC reopening.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in seventeen of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so a score that measures failed mean reversion has almost no path to measure across this horizon. Second, the last observable session was orderly and two-way rather than one-way: the cash range spanned only 159.61 points, the close finished about 105 points below the session high, and VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84. Third, none of the amplifiers that would justify a higher Tail is observed, because observing them requires a live tape. The severity of the oil and shipping picture is therefore carried in Stress at 61 rather than in Tail, consistent with the repository definition that Stress describes a difficult but potentially recoverable environment. The narrow danger window runs from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 01:00 UTC on Monday, where the scheduled restart could produce a gap into thin liquidity; those three slots carry conditional Tail of 22, 21 and 20 and map to WATCH.
headline: Nearly thirty-three hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while Iranian state media report two explosions off Qeshm Island inside the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi authorities say a Houthi attack wounded two people in Jizan, the Saudi East-West pipeline stays shut with 4 to 5 per cent of global oil supply off its route, WTI sits at $100.05 and prediction markets price the 16 September FOMC near 79.5 per cent for a rate increase.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91 per cent, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the session high, roughly 4.5 per cent under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The last quote is timestamped 11 September at 17:15 New York time. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.84 close, inside a 15.59 to 17.71 range, a notably calm volatility print against this macro backdrop. The front Nasdaq-100 futures contract was independently confirmed this hour at a last price of 29,387.00, up 0.86 per cent, and is shown as closed, which corroborates the halt from a second venue rather than from the cash index alone. Rates and oil are equally static: the Federal Reserve H.15 release still carries its 10 September observation at 4.56 per cent for the 2-year, 4.95 per cent for the 10-year and 5.37 per cent for the 30-year, while WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent, and Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent, after Iranian state media said Tehran would meet Gulf states in Oman to discuss the Strait of Hormuz.

What moved in the last hour is the escalation record rather than any price. Iranian state media, reported independently by two outlets, said two explosions were heard off Qeshm Island coming from the direction of the sea, which places reported activity inside the Hormuz chokepoint itself; Iran's president framed the incident in war-crime terms. Saudi civil defence said a Houthi attack wounded two people and damaged a mosque in Jizan, and Houthi forces claimed drone and missile strikes on a Saudi military base while Yemeni government forces counter-attacked around Mokha. The structural picture behind those increments is unchanged: the East-West pipeline, which had been moving 4 to 5 million barrels a day and represents 4 to 5 per cent of global supply, remains shut after a drone attack launched from Iraq's Maysan province, and the International Energy Agency puts Saudi crude supply at its lowest in more than three decades. Houthi forces hold Perim island and both Bab el-Mandeb lanes, a route that carried about 8.1 million barrels a day in the second quarter. On Saturday the U.S. president said he expects the war to end soon after the November midterms and that the Houthis are letting most ships through, a de-escalation signal that sits against the reported strikes rather than resolving them.

The reason this severity is held in Stress rather than Tail is that Tail measures a pathological price path. No such path exists to be measured: there is no live tape, no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme to hold. Prediction markets price a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC near 79.5 per cent after August producer prices rose 0.4 per cent on the month and 5.4 per cent on the year, but that meeting and Wednesday's retail sales both sit beyond this horizon and function as checkpoints rather than priced outcomes. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run and is not used: its payload is stamped 01:28 UTC, well beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, and it reports a partial collection with the economic calendar unavailable, so the assessment rests entirely on independent primary-source research. The scheduled 22:00 UTC restart is the one genuine structural checkpoint inside the horizon, and it is treated as a conditional watch-band window rather than as an observed event.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 05:00 UTC on 12 September to 04:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail opened at 5, stepped to 6 at 09:00 UTC and held there for the rest of the window, in normal mode throughout, tracking the closure rather than any directional view; every slot mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress described a shallow arc, easing from 58 to a 50 low at 17:00 UTC as Friday's crude pullback and the Oman talks headline were absorbed, then rebuilding through 52, 53, 56 and 57 to 60 by the close of the window as attention turned to the restart and to the weekend escalation reports. Confidence held an 85 to 87 band, its dip to 85 through the middle of the window reflecting distance from the last print rather than any loss of verified data. Nothing in the window revised a past opinion with later information.
outlookSummary: Seventeen of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract is scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's eighteenth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 7 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as the interval without price discovery lengthens and unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It steps to 22 in the restart hour, then eases to 21 and 20 as two-way flow is assumed to return, and falls back through 19 and 18 to 17 by the close of the horizon. Those three watch-band slots define the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 01:00 UTC on Monday. Stress eases a point to 60 through the quiet Sunday stretch, then builds to a 66 peak at the restart on the unresolved supply-route picture, the record diesel print and thin reopening liquidity, before decaying to 62 across the Asian session. Confidence declines from 87 to 81 as distance from the last verified print grows, then recovers to 85 once a live tape exists again. Mode stays normal through the closure, is treated as event/whipsaw for the first two restart hours, mixed while early flow is assumed to normalise, and normal again by the end of the horizon. Monday's Salalah meeting between GCC and Iraqi foreign ministers and Iran, Tuesday's Empire State index and Wednesday's retail sales and FOMC decision all sit at or beyond the edge of this horizon and are treated as checkpoints rather than as priced outcomes.
